subject: Medix AI — request to finalize usage adj. and one-off invoice
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@medix.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Medix AI Billing <billing@medix.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected Nov usage spike & request for reconciliation

Hi Connor,

We noticed a substantial one-off charge on the Nov invoice that looks like retroactive consumption for in-product experimentation. Attached is our internal usage export (medix_usage_nov2026.csv) — you can see several high-throughput jobs that started Nov 17 and ran longer than we expected.

This pushed us ~42% over our committed capacity and generated a one-time invoice that will materially affect our Q4 spend. Before I escalate this to procurement, can Redwood help reconcile whether those runs were correctly billed (we believe some may have been double-batched) and consider a one-time make-good or credit? We value the platform but need to avoid a surprise charge that jeopardizes our renewal conversation.

Would appreciate a reconciliation and a suggested remediation (partial credit or invoice adjustment). Happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramos
VP Product
Medix AI
attachments: medix_usage_nov2026.csv

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@medix.ai>
Cc: Medix AI Billing <billing@medix.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected Nov usage spike & request for reconciliation

Hi Sofia — thanks for the heads up and for sending the export. I pulled the attachment and started a quick pass on our side.

Quick summary from my initial look:
- There were a handful of long-running jobs around Nov 17–19 from an API key tied to an internal staging project.
- The runtime pattern suggests those jobs weren’t using the KV cache effectively (higher per-token cost).
- I’ve attached a short breakdown (redwood_overage_breakdown_nov2026.pdf) that maps the top 3 heavy jobs to timestamps from your CSV.

I want to escalate to our billing team for a formal reconciliation and to discuss a one-time remediation. Would you be open to either: (A) a partial credit against the Nov invoice + a small one-time invoice reduction, or (B) a credit plus rolling a portion of the excess into committed capacity for the renewal term? Either way, we’ll get you a clear number.

If you’re free tomorrow at 10am PT I can bring finance on the call.

—Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_overage_breakdown_nov2026.pdf

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Medix AI — unexpected Nov usage spike (need credit approval)

Laura / Marissa — forwarding a thread with Medix (DEAL-7829). Customer found a ~42% overage on Nov that appears tied to a staging project that ran prolonged jobs. I attached their CSV and my quick mapping.

Customer asks: reconciliation and a one-time remediation to avoid blowing the renewal.

Proposal I’d like to discuss:
- Apply a one-time credit equal to 35% of the net overage charge (we estimate overage = $42,300; credit would be ~$14,805)
- Reissue the Nov invoice with the credit applied (invoice INV-2026-MEDIX-12)
- Offer to roll up to 10% of the overage into committed capacity for their next term (to reduce churn risk)

If finance approves, I’ll update the customer and add language to the renewal amendment. Would you prefer a different percentage, or should we route this through sales credits process?

Quoted for context:
> On Mon, Dec 14, 2026 at 09:21 AM Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@medix.ai> wrote:
> > We noticed a substantial one-off charge on the Nov invoice that looks like retroactive consumption ...

Thanks — Connor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 10:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Medix AI — unexpected Nov usage spike (need credit approval)

Connor / Laura — reviewed Medix export and your breakdown. I ran the usage through our billing adjudication flow and confirmed two things:
1) There is an anomalous spike tied to a project id that our logs mark as a long batch (not typical production traffic).
2) Some of the billed tokens were captured at higher cost due to cache-miss behavior (you flagged this).

Recommended remediation (approved):
- Approve a one-time credit equal to 35% of the calculated overage (credit = $14,805).
- Reissue the Nov invoice with the credit and mark invoice status as 'adjusted' in our billing system. I created a draft invoice for review: invoice_draft_MEDIX_202612.pdf (see link).
- Offer the customer a 10% boost to committed capacity for their next 12-month renewal at no additional charge (one-time roll-forward, non-transferable).

Operational notes for Connor:
- Finance will need a signed amendment for the capacity roll-forward and the invoice adjustment. I can attach the amended invoice once we have DocuSign confirmation.
- I scheduled the invoice reissue for 2026-12-18 to avoid end-of-period rush; if Medix needs it sooner, tell me.

Marissa Cole
Revenue Operations 
Redwood Inference
attachments: invoice_draft_MEDIX_202612.pdf

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@medix.ai>, Lucas Tennant <lucas.tennant@medix.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Medix AI Billing <billing@medix.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected Nov usage spike & request for reconciliation — outcome and next steps

Hi Sofia / Lucas — thanks for your patience. Quick update and next steps:

What we found
- Confirmed a non-production batch spike Nov 17–19 that produced the majority of the excess usage.

What we’re doing
- Redwood will apply a one-time credit of $14,805 to the Nov invoice (INV-2026-MEDIX-12). The updated invoice (invoice_draft_MEDIX_202612.pdf) will be reissued on 2026-12-18.
- As a gesture to smooth your renewal, we’ll add a 10% committed capacity credit for your next 12-month term (details in the amendment).

Actions we need from you
1) Please review the attached invoice draft and the amendment outline. I’ve included a DocuSign link for the amendment here: amendment_term_change_docu_sign_link.txt
2) If you want the invoice issued earlier than the 18th, tell me by EOD Monday and we’ll accelerate.

If you’d like a quick 20-min call to walk through the numbers, I can do 10am PT Monday. Otherwise, once the signed amendment is back we’ll push the credit and reissue the invoice.

Appreciate the partnership — we want to make renewals frictionless.

—Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: invoice_draft_MEDIX_202612.pdf, amendment_term_change_docu_sign_link.txt
